history.period: at least ~800-1,000 years old (sources vary; menhirs and ritual stones over 900 years old reported — verify)
history.summary: NOT A HINDU TEMPLE — keep-or-drop decision needed. This is a Khasi indigenous sacred landscape, not a Hindu shrine. The Mawphlang Sacred Grove (Law Kyntang / Law Lyngdoh), ~80-193 acres about 25-27 km southwest of Shillong, has been protected for centuries by the people of Hima Mawphlang under religious taboo: cutting a tree or branch is forbidden, and nothing — not even a twig — may be removed. It is the abode of the deity U Ryngkew U Basa (Labasa), revered by the Chief and elders; the office of Hima Mawphlang, with men of 12 clans (the 'Khadar Kur'), decides all matters of the grove. The forest holds coronation and sacrificial sites marked with monoliths, where Khasi chiefs were anointed; rituals before major community decisions were once held inside, later shifted to a nearby hill. It shelters ~450 species of trees and plants (English yew, Chinese sumac, Japanese blue oak, etc.) plus clouded leopards, monkeys, deer and frogs. CSV 'state' column wrongly holds the town name; real state is MEGHALAYA. Tradition: Khasi indigenous religion (Niam Khasi/Niamtre).

name: Mawphlang Sacred Grove Shrine
town_description: Mawphlang is a village in the East Khasi Hills district, about 25 km from Shillong ('maw phlang' means 'grassy stone'). Besides the sacred grove it is the centre of the 1890s Welsh Presbyterian mission and medical work, and is home to the Khasi Heritage Village.
